answer.rationale: The situation is very similar to day 18 (memory_b1): a recent release coinciding with latency/error spike; a rollback resolved the issue cleanly with no customer impact. Today: p99 write latency is 5× target, started ~90 minutes ago, and the release went out 2 hours ago — the timeline strongly suggests the release is the causal driver. Settlement writes are at daily peak, but rolling back to the prior known-stable build is the fastest, lowest-risk way to restore write-path health without losing customer writes (writes continue, just on the stable build). Circuit breakers (memory_b4) address partner outages, not latency regressions. Regional failover (memory_b2) is heavier-handed and risks transient write loss during cutover. Adding capacity (memory_b3) helps when demand exceeds supply, but 5× latency with a coincident release points to a code regression, not load. Routing reads to replicas (memory_b5) targets read/query load, not write-path p99. One intervention only: rollback the release now.
